material_defects.title: Forwarded unsafe requests have no target-cache invalidation obligation

locators: section 6 Alternatives and non-cached requests, line 94

material_defects.observed: The complete final passes non-GET requests through and does not cache their responses. It never specifies invalidation of existing GET entries on receiving a successful response to an unsafe/unknown-safety method, and its proposed tests omit that transition. Treatment account-session invalidation is unrelated to target-URI protocol invalidation.

authority.locator: RFC 9111 section 4.4, pinned text lines 1020-1049; adjacent section 4 write-through rule and RFC 9110 section 9.2.1

material_defects.governing_condition: The cache receives a 2xx or 3xx response to a forwarded unsafe request (including unknown-safety methods). It must invalidate the target URI; optional additional Location/Content-Location invalidation has a same-origin limit. GET-only storage does not remove this rule.
material_defects.consequence: A fresh stored GET can continue satisfying later reads after a successful state-changing request through this component. Omitting the transition leaves the proposed cache coherent only by an unstated assumption about callers.
material_defects.planning_example: An eligible GET /doc is stored with a positive freshness lifetime. DELETE /doc is forwarded through the stated pass-through path and returns 204. The proposal leaves no stated mandatory-validation/removal transition for /doc before a later cached GET.
material_defects.example_status: Static source-based reasoning; no HTTP client, server fixture or implementation was executed.
material_defects.applicability_limit: The brief chiefly describes GET browsing. The omission is graded on the final itself explicitly forwarding non-GET/unsafe requests, rather than requiring the reader to add write features or build a whole client. A truly separate enforced GET-only API would require a different stated boundary; it is not assumed from this artifact.
material_defects.confidence: HIGH for the normative rule and omission; explicit applicability boundary retained for any separate adjudication
material_defects.original_grade_effect: source FAIL; no prospective execution or deployment demanded

nonmaterial_findings_and_limits.text: Library suitability, client integration, OS key/storage guarantees and real offline/performance behavior remain unknown. These are proposed validations, not reasons to invent an execution failure.

Exact artifact write completion, queue/start/provider-active phases, full context occupancy and billed resource breakdown are unavailable in the assigned frozen records. No native transcript was opened.

Export survives only as a future user-requested action separated from HTTP caching. The draft/critique explicit provenance/account/privacy governance and no-relabeling language are not restated. This is a finite preservation weakness, graded nonmaterial because no export implementation is proposed and the cache reuse prohibitions themselves are retained.

The private row does not explain the field-qualified shared-cache exception and uses an unqualified shared-storage prohibition. Dispositions F1 explicitly say unqualified private. Own private-cache behavior is correct; shared cache is outside scope, so this wording/scope loss is not the decisive failure.

all_supplied_criticism_dispositions.reason: no-cache storage/reuse distinction, qualified no-cache conservative whole-response policy, private-user-agent storage, must-understand/status/no-store exception and unimplemented status gate retained.
Vary star/absence/normalization rules and full corrected age replace the false draft rules; fresh reuse and conservative unreliable-clock handling retained.
No offline bypass for no-cache/stale must-revalidate; eligible stale use and unavailable states remain. Export compression is separately reported for treatment.
Eligible 304 candidate set and strong/weak/absent-validator selection; supplied metadata, Content-Length/processing exceptions, body ownership and unconditional fallback retained.

Single-user GET cache, accounts/sign-out/redaction, bytes/encoding, bounded LRU/atomic generations, library/custom/live alternatives and retired URL-only history retained. No implementation/audit/witness is fabricated.
